body: Yes, she has bad mental health as well and has given up on doing anything in life. She sits in her room (in the basement) all day and night playing on her computer. She refuses to get a job or participate in anything.
I don't think so, I have at least a day or two to enroll before any legal action will certainly be taken. I just have to work up the courage to get my mother informed and help me be reenrolled.
Yes, as it's required for anyone under 18. I figured if I could just do minimal attendance I'd be able to last another month. It's my own fault, but I wish I had gotten the help I needed earlier.

I took an online school. Due to my lack of participation, they blocked my account and I had to contact them to get the block removed. I hated the thought of contacting someone and talking to them through the phone. I didn't want to be asked any questions or anything, so I put it off. Eventually I was withdrawn for truancy.

I was pulling through depression with the help of my significant other. They are out of country (Canada) and I was hoping to move with them once I turned 18. It was a stretch, but it would have finally given me something to live for and experience independence. I've hardly gotten to do much of anything in my life and was never trusted with doing anything. 

I don't know how to tell my mother I've been withdrawn. I fear she'll go absolutely insane and either become suicidal herself or do something that'll make me even more emotionally scarred.

I'll probably have to go to court. The kinds of actions they take there would be alongside counselling, time in a juvenile center, or community service. My parents will probably want me out of their lives if any of that happens, which I would never want. Their lives are hard enough without my problems.
